clue.text: Seize greeting card!

parts.note: hi is an informal word of greeting
a jack is a court card in a pack of playing cards

explanation.surface: An excited instruction to grab a greetings card.
explanation.definitionFit: To hijack something is to take control of it by force, a vivid synonym for seizing it.

clue.text: Attend to layer protecting English ship

indicators.note: protecting means the outer word wraps round the others as a shield

parts.note: a hen is a bird that lays eggs, a layer
the ark is Noah's vessel, a ship

explanation.surface: A protective coating is wanted for a British ship's hull.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearken is an old word for listening closely, which is attending to something.

clue.text: Very happy

definitions.meaning: in informal British speech ... means very, as in ... good
... as an adjective means cheerful and merry

explanation.definitionFit: Jolly works both as a British intensifier meaning extremely and as an adjective for cheerful.

clue.text: Quote about promotion supported by Leninite leader in the Kremlin

indicators.note: in a down clue, supported by means the next piece sits underneath
about means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: to quote is to cite
an ad, advertisement, is a promotion

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone cites a remark about advancement endorsed by a Leninist chief in Moscow.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kremlin is the fortified complex in Moscow, a classic example of a citadel.

clue.text: Buy shares, perhaps, though seen to have lost shirt?

definitions.meaning: to put money into stocks; buying shares is one example
someone seen in just an undergarment has lost their shirt, also slang for losing money

explanation.surface: A punter considers putting money in stocks despite the risk of losing everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost shirt' is the slang for losing all one's money, which suits investing; read literally, someone without a shirt is seen in a vest.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest is to commit money to shares in hope of profit; the second reading splits the word into in and vest.

clue.text: The labourers in front set up contests

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: the van is the front, as in vanguard
vies means competes or contests

explanation.surface: Workers at the head of a queue arrange competitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Navvies are manual labourers, originally those who dug canals and railways in Britain.

clue.text: I matter, so poor a country

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters are in bad shape and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone protests that their plight is important, a poor country being their case.
explanation.definitionFit: East Timor is a south-east Asian nation, independent since 2002, so a country by name.

clue.text: Oz following on after opener in test gaining runs, bringing defeat

indicators.note: gaining means the first letter collects the next piece right beside it
following on after means this piece comes after the others
opener in means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
oz is the abbreviation for ounce

explanation.surface: An Australian side follows on in a cricket test, piles up runs but still loses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oz' looks like Australia; it is the weight abbreviation. 'Following on' is a cricket term for batting again straight after a big deficit.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce someone is to defeat them heavily.

clue.text: Careless to cut into eye

indicators.note: into means one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: to eye is to watch or spy
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: Someone clumsily cuts close to an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloppy work is careless, done without proper attention.

clue.text: Neither radio nor wireless!

parts.note: a broadcast medium that is not sound-only like radio and not over the air, since it comes down a wire

explanation.definitionFit: This service delivers pictures as well as sound, through wires rather than over the air.

clue.text: Funny Peter appearing in dictionary, it's granted

indicators.note: appearing in means one name is placed inside the other

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
Peter Kay is a British stand-up comedian

explanation.surface: A comedian gets an entry in the dictionary, a privilege allowed him.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Kay is a popular comedian from northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something okayed has been approved, so permission has been granted.

clue.text: Boobs on page three, perhaps

parts.note: boobs as blunders that appear on a newspaper page, not the topless model of the Sun's notorious page three

explanation.walkthrough: The Sun, a British tabloid, long printed a topless model on page three, which is the surface the clue plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Typographical slips in a newspaper are mistakes, colloquially boobs, made in what is set and published.

clue.text: Girl approaches university friend every so often

indicators.note: approaches means the girl comes up to, and stands before, what follows

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A girl walks up to her college friend from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: Annually means once a year, a regular interval loosely described as every so often.

clue.text: Where teeth filed, one finds hidden colour

parts.note: in an alphabetical index, teeth would be filed under the letter T
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dentist filing teeth uncovers a concealed shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filed' suggests a dentist's file; it means put in a filing system, where teeth go under T.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertone is a subdued colour showing through another, a hidden tint.

clue.text: With less fat, pound off stew

indicators.note: off means the named letter is taken away

parts.note: slimmer means having less fat
L is the abbreviation for pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A dieter loses some weight while cooking a stew.
explanation.definitionFit: To simmer is to cook gently just below the boil, as one does with a stew.

clue.text: Poor stiff, finished

parts.note: hard means stiff, unbending
up means finished, as in time is up

explanation.surface: A poor stiff, a hapless fellow, is all washed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard up is an idiom for being short of money, that is, poor.

clue.text: He's studied what blows smoke through hole

indicators.note: through means one word is put inside the other

parts.note: the anus is a bodily opening, a hole
a lum is a Scottish and northern word for a chimney, which sends smoke up

explanation.surface: A description of a pipe blowing smoke out of an opening.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumnus is a former student of a school or university, someone who has studied there.

clue.text: Injection of drug? Crack

indicators.note: of means the injection is of the drug, so the drug comes first

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis
a shot is an injection

explanation.surface: A user asks about a shot of drugs before mentioning crack cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like the drug; it is a try, as in having a crack at something.
explanation.definitionFit: A potshot is a casual attempt, just as a crack is a try at something.

clue.text: Heading for drink such as this, sadly

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: points back at the drink: oloroso is a dark sweet sherry, a drink of that kind

explanation.surface: Someone heads for a drink of this kind with a sorrowful air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such as this' refers to the drink just named: oloroso is a type of sherry.
explanation.definitionFit: Doloroso is the Italian musical direction to play sorrowfully, that is, sadly.

clue.text: European was obliged to admit crime, suffering fate of Mussolini?

indicators.note: Mussolini's body was hung upside down, so in a down clue the letters are turned bottom to top
to admit means one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: had, as in had to, means was obliged
sin is a crime or wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Someone forced to confess suffers a dictator's grisly end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering fate of Mussolini' turns HSINAD upside down: Mussolini's corpse was hung by the heels in Milan in 1945.
explanation.definitionFit: A Danish person comes from Denmark, so is European.

clue.text: Oval object that is secured by both sides with longer pins

indicators.note: secured by means the outer letters hold the others between them

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right, the two sides
an egg is an oval object
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: An oval item is fixed on either side by longer pins.
explanation.definitionFit: Pins is slang for legs, so someone with longer pins is leggier.

clue.text: Son in first relationship, but still a virgin?

parts.note: anyone in their first relationship has no former partner, no ex, so is without an ex

explanation.surface: A boy is in his first romance yet has not slept with anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse needs a coined word: in a first relationship you have no ex, so you are ex-less.
explanation.definitionFit: A virgin has never had intercourse, so a virgin's life has been without sex.

clue.text: Month spent with rogue, popular though cheesy

parts.note: Aug is the abbreviation for August
a rat is a scoundrel or rogue
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A month passed with a popular scoundrel, though it was all rather cheesy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheesy' looks like tacky; it means topped with cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish served au gratin is topped with browned breadcrumbs and cheese, hence cheesy.

clue.text: Festival axes a lot of stars

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration
x and y are the two axes on a graph

explanation.surface: A celebration chops down lots of film stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axes' looks like a verb meaning cuts; it is the plural noun, the x and y axes of a graph.
explanation.definitionFit: A galaxy is a huge system containing a vast number of stars.

clue.text: Some diagonal lines drawn up, it's plain to see

indicators.note: in a down clue, drawn up means the letters read bottom to top
some means only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: Some diagonal lines are sketched, and the picture is easy to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn up' turns ONALL, found inside 'diagonal lines', bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a broad treeless grassy plain in South America.

clue.text: Bizarre finale to paint nudes pistachio green

indicators.note: bizarre means the letters are put in a strange new order
finale to means the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An odd artistic finish has nudes painted in pistachio green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' looks like the colour after 'pistachio'; it means naive. 'Bizarre' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Green in the sense of inexperienced or naive means unsophisticated.

clue.text: Joggers get so horribly wet, say

indicators.note: horribly means the letters are badly mangled and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Runners end up dreadfully damp, as one might say.
explanation.definitionFit: Joggers become sweaty through exertion, so the phrase describes their state rather than naming a synonym.

clue.text: See 11
